description: We are Foul & Fire, three teammates from Cairo who mix data, code, and design (and a love for a good plate of foul). Our project, Burnwise, turns 20+ years of MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire data into one consistent burning activity calendar, helping emergency managers and scientists spot unusual fire seasons and respond faster.
summary:
Burnwise is an interactive fire-monitoring platform that transforms NASA satellite fire detections into a consistent historical record to help identify unusual fire activity and support early warning.

The project addresses a major challenge: MODIS and VIIRS satellites detect fires at different spatial resolutions, creating artificial jumps when their data are combined. Burnwise harmonizes both datasets using a Random Forest model and a statistical ratio baseline, producing a monthly fire record from 2003 to 2026.

Users can explore fire activity through an interactive map, a monthly burning calendar, historical comparisons, anomaly alerts, and high-risk fire clusters. The platform also supports CSV exports for further analysis.

Focusing on Egypt and the Nile Delta, Burnwise aims to support environmental monitoring, emergency planning, and understanding seasonal agricultural burning and its impact on air quality.
details:
How Burnwise Works

Burnwise is an end-to-end satellite fire-monitoring and analytics platform designed to provide a reliable historical view of vegetation fire activity.

1. Data Collection and Processing

We collected historical active-fire detections from NASA FIRMS, using MODIS Collection 6.1 and VIIRS S-NPP 375m datasets. The data were cleaned by removing duplicates, filtering non-vegetation detections, applying confidence thresholds, and aggregating fire counts into a 0.25° spatial grid with monthly resolution.

2. Cross-Sensor Harmonization

Since MODIS and VIIRS have different detection resolutions and sensitivities, combining their raw observations can produce misleading trends. We developed two harmonization approaches:

  • A statistical baseline using a constant VIIRS/MODIS ratio.
  • A Random Forest model trained on the 2013–2022 overlapping period.

The Random Forest achieved a 9.1% leave-one-year-out yearly error, compared with 17.6% for the ratio baseline.

3. Interactive Monitoring and Analytics

The web application allows users to:

  • Select geographic areas and date ranges through an interactive map.
  • Explore a 283-month historical burning calendar covering January 2003 to July 2026.
  • Compare current fire activity against historical monthly medians.
  • Receive anomaly alerts using robust statistical scoring.
  • Identify and visualize high-risk fire clusters using HDBSCAN.
  • Export selected monthly fire data as CSV files.

Impact and Innovation

Burnwise makes satellite fire data easier to understand and use without requiring advanced GIS expertise. It can support environmental researchers, emergency managers, and land managers in identifying unusual burning patterns, understanding seasonal agricultural fires, and improving resource planning.

The project focuses on the Nile Delta, where agricultural residue burning contributes to seasonal air pollution and the autumn black cloud phenomenon.

Technologies Used

Python, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, Random Forest, SHAP, HDBSCAN, Google Colab, FastAPI, JavaScript, Leaflet, Leaflet Draw, and Chart.js.

Creative Approach

Our main innovation is combining cross-sensor data harmonization, transparent model validation, historical anomaly detection, and spatial clustering in one accessible platform. We also openly report model limitations and compare our results against simpler baselines rather than presenting machine learning performance without context.
